name: Maine
lawPassed: 2021, under An Act To Support and Improve Municipal Recycling Programs and Save Taxpayer Money (LD 1541).
status: Implementation is underway; Maine updated the law in 2025, expects producer registration/data reporting in May 2026 and first annual payments in September 2027 for 2026 packaging.
milestones: Fees tied to volume/type of packaging. SO not yet selected as of mid-2026; RFP issued June 15, 2026.

name: Washington
lawPassed: 2025, under SB 5284 (the Recycling Reform Act, or WRAP Act).
status: Rulemaking, program design and early implementation underway.
milestones: PRO appointed by Jan 1 2026; registration with Ecology by Mar 1 2026; supply report due May 31 2026; producer participation required by July 1 2026.

name: Oregon
lawPassed: 2021, under the Plastic Pollution and Recycling Modernization Act (SB 582).

milestones: Fees by material/recyclability/volume. Feb 2026: federal injunction for NAW members; trial July 13, 2026. DEQ published ~300 non-compliant producers Apr 9, 2026, fines up to $25k/day.

name: Maryland

milestones: CAA registration by July 1 2026; simplified supply report (2025 data) due May 31 2026; covered materials list by July 1 2027; full plans due July 1 2028.

name: California
lawPassed: California SB 54 (Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act, signed 2022) — permanent implementing regulations finalized May 1, 2026; enforcement obligations active; CAA draft program plan submitted June 15, 2026; federal constitutional challenge filed June 22, 2026 (Nebraska v. Heller); law remains in effect pending court action.
status: Permanent SB 54 regulations took effect May 1, 2026 upon OAL approval, triggering producer registration and reporting obligations (initial deadline June 1, 2026). CAA submitted its draft California Program Plan to the SB 54 Advisory Board on June 15, 2026, opening a public comment period through August 14, 2026, with a final plan due to CalRecycle in October 2026 and full program implementation targeted for January 1, 2027. On June 22, 2026, a coalition of 17 state attorneys general led by Nebraska, joined by the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors, filed a federal lawsuit (Nebraska v. Heller, E.D. Cal.) challenging SB 54 on Commerce Clause, First Amendment, and other constitutional grounds; the suit does not automatically suspend the law and no injunction has been issued.
milestones: June 30, 2022 — Governor Newsom signed SB 54 into law
March 7, 2025 — Governor Newsom directed CalRecycle to restart rulemaking over cost concerns
May 1, 2026 — OAL approved and filed permanent SB 54 regulations; took effect immediately
June 1, 2026 — Producer registration and baseline 2023 supply data submission deadline (CAA or CalRecycle)
June 2, 2026 — NRDC/Californians Against Waste/Oceana filed state court lawsuit challenging certain regulatory provisions (advanced recycling exemptions)
June 15, 2026 — CAA submitted draft California Program Plan to SB 54 Advisory Board; public comment open through August 14, 2026
June 22, 2026 — 17-state coalition + NAW filed federal lawsuit Nebraska v. Heller challenging SB 54 constitutionality; no injunction issued
August 14, 2026 — Public comment deadline on CAA draft program plan
October 2026 — CAA to submit final program plan to CalRecycle
January 1, 2027 — Full EPR program implementation targeted; $500M/year producer fee regime to begin

name: Colorado
lawPassed: Colorado HB22-1355 (Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act), signed June 3, 2022, covering all packaging materials and paper products (including poly bags, plastic film, paper, and other flexible/rigid packaging). The program entered active implementation as of January 1, 2026, with producer dues obligations live. Within the last 30 days, the ILMA lawsuit against CDPHE (filed March 12, 2026) remains pending in Denver District Court with no injunction in place, and SB26-192 (EPR dues appeal bill) was introduced in the 2026 session but did not advance to enactment before the legislature adjourned May 13, 2026.
status: Colorado's EPR program is fully live: producers of all covered packaging and paper products have been required to register with CAA since October 2024, submit supply reports (2024 data due July 31, 2025; 2025 data due May 31, 2026), and pay annual dues beginning January 2026. CDPHE approved CAA's final program plan on December 9, 2025, with CAA required to begin full implementation by June 9, 2026. A legal challenge by the Independent Lubricant Manufacturers Association (ILMA) filed March 12, 2026 in Denver District Court alleges constitutional and statutory violations in CDPHE's program implementation; no injunction has been issued and the program continues to operate.
milestones: June 3, 2022: Governor Polis signed HB22-1355 into law
May 2023: CDPHE designated Circular Action Alliance (CAA) as the state PRO
June 14, 2024: Solid and Hazardous Waste Commission adopted final Section 18 producer regulations
October 1, 2024: Producer registration deadline with CAA
July 1, 2025: Prohibition on selling/distributing covered materials without program participation took effect
July 31, 2025: Initial supply report deadline (2024 data)
September 2025: CDPHE approved Interchange 360's individual program plan for automotive lubricant packaging
November 2025: Solid and Hazardous Waste Commission adopted eco-modulation ruleset (Section 18 amendments)
December 9, 2025: CDPHE approved CAA's final program plan
January 2026: Producer dues obligations began
March 12, 2026: ILMA filed lawsuit in Denver District Court challenging CDPHE's EPR implementation (no injunction issued; program continues)
March 13, 2026: Interchange 360 began implementation for automotive lubricant packaging
May 13, 2026: Colorado legislature adjourned; SB26-192 (EPR dues appeal bill, sponsored by Sen. Cutter) failed to advance to enactment
June 9, 2026: Deadline for CAA to begin full program plan implementation
May 31, 2026: 2025 annual supply report deadline for producers

name: Connecticut
lawPassed: Connecticut has no enacted EPR packaging law. Two successive packaging EPR-related bills failed to advance: HB 6917 (2025 session) died on the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, and HB 5151 (2026 session) died in committee. Connecticut's 2026 legislative session has adjourned without passing packaging EPR legislation.
status: HB 6917, a solid-waste omnibus bill that included a mandate to study the need and viability of packaging EPR by January 15, 2027, passed the House in the 2025 session but was tabled on the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, the final day of session, and died there. In the 2026 session, HB 5151—introduced February 11, 2026—would have required the state to submit EPR program proposals derived from a waste characterization study, but it died in committee before the 2026 session ended. A separate packaging-related bill, HB 5524 (polystyrene and PFAS-straw ban), also died in committee in the 2026 session. Connecticut has enacted a postconsumer recycled content requirement for plastic beverage containers (HB 6664, 2023) and an EPR law for consumer batteries (HB 5019, 2025), but no comprehensive packaging EPR program.
milestones: 2023: HB 6664 signed into law — EPR for packaging stripped before passage; recycled content mandate (25% by 2027, 30% by 2032) for plastic beverage containers enacted
2025 session: HB 6917 (packaging EPR feasibility study) passed House, tabled on Senate calendar June 4, 2025 — died without a Senate vote
2025: HB 5019 signed into law — EPR for consumer batteries enacted (not packaging)
2026 session: HB 5151 (packaging EPR recommendations from waste characterization study) introduced February 11, 2026 — died in committee when 2026 session ended
2026 session: HB 5524 (polystyrene/PFAS-straw ban) died in committee — 2026 session adjourned with no packaging EPR advancement
